summary: Dream's first solo single, and the loudest reaction is to the MV's male lead Yin, whose own followers arrive to say so — his looks and playfulness get more comment volume than the track. The second cluster is pride in the solo debut itself, framed as a progression from the trio single to having her own song, and praising her as an all-rounder who dances, sings and acts. A clear, repeated request is for her to try a slow ballad, with several commenters saying her tone suits it and one hearing a 90s Thai pop quality in it. Industry peers are present in the thread: the songwriter from Tilly Birds thanks the channel for the commission, and marr team publicly pitch a collaboration. A running joke notes the MV lead was cast to resemble her real-life partner, with some asking why he wasn't cast instead.

audience_signals: The channel now functions as an industry node — the songwriter (Tilly Birds) and another act (marr team) are in the comments, and collaboration requests are arriving inbound rather than being sought
Per-member solo releases work as a growth path; the audience immediately asks for a genre pivot rather than more of the same
Casting a popular actor as MV lead imports his fandom wholesale and shifts the comment mix away from the music
Members' real relationships are openly used by the audience as casting subtext, so the line between programme and personal life is already blurred by choice
The near-total absence of criticism on member solo work suggests goodwill is transferable from the group to the individual
content_requests: Cast her real partner in the next MV
